title: Optimization observability and decision artifacts
description:
Purpose: Make optimization progress, evidence, decisions, and partial failures understandable to operators and machine-checkable by other agents.

Exclusions:
- Persisting full client content in logs or Kanbus.
- Alternate metric calculations that diverge from final evaluation reports.
- UI redesign unrelated to optimization observability.

Dependencies: Defines a shared run-evidence contract consumed by execution, safety, and orchestration. Contract work may proceed independently.

Definition of Done:
- Structured status identifies current phase, completed phases, active evaluations, progress, and terminal state.
- Decision artifacts preserve cohort provenance, candidate lineage, metrics, validation gates, failures, and selection rationale.
- Compact summaries agree with final report metrics.
- Partial failures remain visible without discarding successful evidence.
- Operator handoff output is concise and actionable.
- Behavior-first specifications and focused tests pass.

Running log: Record sanitized decisions, attempts, outcomes, and next steps in this epic or its child issues.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Decision-artifacts work started in an isolated worktree. Scope: make compact optimizer handoff summaries derive metrics, terminal state, candidate lineage, cohort provenance, and visible partial failures from final report evidence; add focused behavior-first tests; avoid duplicate issue creation.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implemented and verified a final-report-authoritative optimizer handoff contract. Compact artifacts now retain selected-candidate and current-leader evidence, cohort provenance, and explicit partial report failures while preserving completed evaluation evidence. Focused artifact and optimizer CLI-result tests pass; validation and scoped commit are next.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Wave 1 integration makes final report evidence authoritative for compact handoff artifacts, preserves selected-candidate and cohort provenance, and surfaces partial report-phase failures without discarding completed evidence. Full supported-runtime and dashboard CI passed.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Dogfood reporting findings: a bounded scoped run safely stopped before semantic diagnosis when the configured model-work cap was lower than the policy-selected set. The Report correctly remained incomplete but did not prominently explain the blocker or next operator action. Design follow-up should add an aggregate overview, expandable scorecard/score hierarchy, revisioned Markdown/CSV artifacts, stable dashboard artifact links, and a visible terminal-blocker card. No client-specific information is recorded here.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Phase-two delivery began under the software delivery team workflow. Recorded behavior stories for exactly-once launch, terminal child waiting, deterministic outcome and contradiction classification, and one-Report lifecycle continuation. Implementation is sequenced as recovery hardening plus an upstream host-neutral wait contract, followed by idempotent child creation and Plexus wait integration, then outcome projection and presentation, independent review, and local/sandbox validation. No schema resources, automatic operational mutation, production optimizer run, commit, push, or deployment is authorized.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Started a sanitized decision-first Report refinement after dogfood evidence showed that exhaustive inventory rows obscured the run conclusion and next actions. The change will separate action aggregates from evidence exploration, distinguish diagnosis deferral from execution rejection, and prevent deferred diagnoses from appearing execution-ready.
